key_insight: FREDI jointly optimizes fair wireless resource allocation and dual-threshold early-exit inference to securely route only critical events from edge devices to an edge server for deeper classification.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical way to balance latency, security, and fairness in cooperative edge AI systems while remaining solvable with certified optimization guarantees.
method: Use dual confidence thresholds on early-exit CNNs at each UE to trigger secure offloading only for critical events.
Formulate a proportional-fair utility maximization over UE–ES association, wireless resources, processing resources, and thresholds.
Decompose the problem into exact threshold search over finite confidence values and a mixed-integer exponential-cone resource-allocation subproblem.
evidence_signal: Experiments with early-exit MobileNetV2 and ShuffleNetV2 report near-perfect UE fairness, aggregate utility close to a Sum-Utility benchmark, and Stage-A scalability from 6 to 144 UEs with median solve time below 0.1 s in tested cases.
watch_item: The approach relies on accurate confidence calibration and problem-specific optimization structure, so deployment may be sensitive to model miscalibration or larger-scale network dynamics not covered in the experiments.
paper_title: Proportional-Fair Resource Allocation and Dual-Threshold Early-Exit Inference for Secure Cooperative Multi-Layer Edge Intelligence
